newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yields close stronger across the curve.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yields close stronger across the curve.

text.p: 0525 GMT
* NZ bonds well supported on continued issuance
* Short end rallies after futures close-out
* Market appears bullish on Friday's RBNZ statement
* Cash at 10.05 pct vs 10.00 pct at Tuesday's close
* 90 day bills 9.86 pct vs 9.91
* 7/98 bond yields 8.00 pct vs 8.07 pct
* 02/01 bond yields 8.22 pct vs 8.27 pct
* 11/06 bond yields 8.28 vs 8.30 pct
* Sept bank bill futures -7 at 90.05, Dec +5 at 90.78
New Zealand debt securities closed with a strong bid tone on Wednesday, with yields between two and seven basis points lower across the curve.
Dealers said 90-day bank bills had rallied after the futures close-out earlier in the session, while the mid-curve bonds were well supported on continued dual-currency issuance.

"There may have been some fairly large positions to close out. I think the local market seemed to be a little shorter than longer, so generally the locals seemed to be quite happy to see rates or futures sold off before futures close and rally straight after that," a dealer said.
He said there appeared to be a bullish expectation creeping into the short end ahead of the Reserve Bank's economic projections on Friday.
"The December futures tell a story -- they're up five or six (points) on the day -- so that's sending out a relatively bullish signal."
Bonds also rallied in light trade, despite a weaker U.S. Treasuries market overnight.
"These Euros, Samurais, duals, they're keeping the middle bond part of the curve well bid," a dealer said.
A NZ$100 million one-year Eurobond was issued by Inter-American Development Bank overnight.
The dealer said the prospects for further strength in the bond market looked good.
"There's still talk of more issues out there, so that's going to keep a bid tone on things in the meantime," he said.
